dimensions.name: Protocol/spec/proof package
dimensions.residualRisk: Package refs can become stale after future implementation changes.
dimensions.scoreRationale: Protocol Omega package and readiness gap assessment exist, but the readiness register itself is the baseline control.

dimensions.name: Verifier/sample/tamper corpus
dimensions.residualRisk: More real-world election shapes and platforms need additional samples.
dimensions.scoreRationale: Protocol package evidence exists, but the public verifier sample and tamper corpus still needs FEAT-135.

dimensions.name: Cross-device receipt/inclusion verification
dimensions.residualRisk: Device loss, offline handling, manual entry, and accessibility edge cases may remain.
dimensions.scoreRationale: Verification direction is known, but FEAT-136 must deliver the cross-device path before pilot claims can open.

dimensions.name: Publication/counting evidence
dimensions.residualRisk: Publication and counting evidence must stay bound to current release and package refs.
dimensions.scoreRationale: EPIC-013 publication/counting evidence exists, with remaining readiness binding handled by this register.

dimensions.name: Per-election KMS custody lifecycle
dimensions.residualRisk: Cloud-provider incidents, IAM drift, regional availability, deployment variants, and limited operating history may remain.
dimensions.scoreRationale: FEAT-131 delivered accepted internal evidence for fail-closed open, finalization cleanup, reconciliation, redaction, and focused verification.

dimensions.name: Trusted deployment ceremony
dimensions.residualRisk: Repeated operating history grows only after more elections.
dimensions.scoreRationale: Release integrity evidence exists, but FEAT-132 must prove the controlled ceremony path.

dimensions.name: Operational evidence package
dimensions.residualRisk: Site-specific monitoring, backup, incident, operator, dependency, and support evidence may vary by deployment.
dimensions.scoreRationale: Operational direction and support/security artifacts exist, but FEAT-133 and FEAT-134 must package repeatable evidence.

dimensions.name: Retention/log privacy proof
dimensions.residualRisk: New diagnostics or observability tools can reintroduce correlation risk without ongoing scans.
dimensions.scoreRationale: FEAT-137 accepted evidence proves the reviewed HushVoting boundary has no durable identity-to-ballot join, guarded in-memory cast behavior, atomic cast proof, and clean log/support/package scan output.

dimensions.name: Dispute/continuity readiness dependency
sourceGapRows: ElectionOwner void decision and publication replacement
dimensions.residualRisk: Customer governance may still decide remedies, deadlines, and authority actions.
dimensions.scoreRationale: Anomaly/dispute direction exists, but FEAT-138 and FEAT-139 must prove void and continuity readiness.

dimensions.name: Pilot/legal/governance delivery wrapper
dimensions.residualRisk: HushVoting can provide the voting subsystem for binding customer decisions when customer-supplied authority and rules support that use, but legal sufficiency, full meeting governance, challenge windows, remedies, and pilot operating evidence remain customer/reviewer owned.
dimensions.scoreRationale: FEAT-140 delivered the accepted legal/governance boundary wrapper with explicit non-legal-validation limits; controlled pilot evidence remains pending.

claimLevels.allowedWording: HushVoting may use this register for internal development tracking and implementation planning.
HushVoting may run an internal non-binding rehearsal when all remaining blockers stay visible.
claimLevels.limitationWording: The rehearsal must be clearly labelled non-binding and must not be presented as customer, production, or public election readiness.

claimLevels.blockedWording: Friendly organization pilot readiness is blocked until the score reaches the minimum confidence band and the remaining pilot-critical red blockers are resolved.
Production organizational rollout is blocked by the v1 claim policy.
Public or state election readiness is blocked by the v1 claim policy.
